articles.text: The Piedmont Recreation Depar tment’s Walking on Wednesdays group had another strong turnout of 29 walkers on November 17. One of the areas they had not visited was the Sandringham/Selborne/Estates/ Inverleith loop near the top of Hampton Avenue. The walkers said they were ready for the challenge, and off they went on one of the longest walk of the year and one with some steep climbs. Before they began, Recreation Department Supervisor Eva Phalen told the walkers about new, unique adult programs developed for 2022. The higher elevation in this section of Piedmont seems to make the color of the leaves on the trees a little more vibrant late in the fall season. Realizing that this might be the last really good Wednesday for fall colors, seeing some beautiful trees was another excellent reason to take this walk. The long line of walkers went up Highland Avenue with Hampton Park their initial destination. They took their usual route down Sheridan and up Wildwood Avenues. A quick passage through the always lovely Hall Fenway took the walkers to Crocker and Hampton Avenues. They went past Crocker Park (also known to locals as Bear Park). then crossed La Salle Avenue, going through the columns that marked the entrance to the early Piedmont St. James Woods neighborhood. The boundaries of this large development are still marked by original, tile inlay sidewalks. The walkers continued their ascent of Hampton and came to a set of trees with striking red leaves that were more vibrant than those of the trees below. The group came to Sandringham and went up to the Marlborough Court cul-desac, and then another half block to Sandringham Place, another cul-de-sac. Along the street there is a medium sized tree whose bunches overhang the sidewalk and create what is almost like a leaf tunnel. When the group came to Selborne Drive they stopped to admire a beautiful, clear view of the Bay in the distance. Going up Selborne took the walkers to Estates Drive and a short climb up to upper and lower Inverleith Terrace. The walkers took Inverleith back to Hampton, and along the way passed liquidambar trees with more vibrant red leaves and a bottlebrush tree with a very active hummingbird. The group went down La Salle and St. James Drive, back to Hampton and retraced their steps to the Exedra. It had been a little over a five-mile walk, the longest Wednesday walk that anyone could remember, but very enjoyable – and probably good preparation for the Turkey Trot on Thanksgiving morning. The Walking on Wednesdays group meets every Wednesday at the Exedra (Highland & Magnolia Avenues) at 10:30 a.m. Everyone is invited to join the group and there is no charge. New walkers and their friendly K-9 best friends are especially welcome. Registration with the Piedmont Recreation Department is required at https://tinyurl. com/3ethkehu. Committee member Eugene Brown said, “appropriate considerations and recommendations have been made and I would look at this as a mid-point in a continually evolving process that will continue to be evaluated and modified as circumstances dictate”. Pursuant to California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Guidelines Section 15072, the city staff prepared an Initial Study for public review. Having received no comments, staff is recommending that City Council adopt a Negative Declaration based on the Initial Study. On Monday, December 6, the City Council will consider adopting a resolution to approve the draft plan. Following adoption, implementation of the Plan’s recommendations, programs and policies will begin. City staff will continue to monitor existing bike and pedestrian traffic conditions in the City. “The Piedmont Safer Streets report is a vital document that will act as a blueprint for prioritizing the locations and the types of bicycle and pedestrian safety improvements over the next five years. Public Works and Engineering look forward to addressing the issues identified at the highest priority locations first and making this community a safer place to walk and bike”, said Daniel Gonzales, City’s Public Works Director. The Final Draft Plan is available for public review on the City’s website. The December 6 City Council meeting agenda and staff report for the Plan will be posted on the City’s website no later than Friday, December 3. articles.text: As of November 30, all but 14 Piedmont students aged 12 and older have provided proof of COVID-19 vaccination to the school district. It equates to a vaccination rate of 99% among the 1,222 students in that age bracket. The deadline to submit proof of vaccination was November 17 and is mandatory to attend school in person. On January 5, 2022, the first day of the second semester, students without proof of vaccination or a medical exemption from a physician, will be referred to independent study. The school district has not received any formal submissions of medical exemptions. “As of [November 30], we are not aware of any student who is definitely opting for Independent Study starting January 5,” said PUSD Communication Director Brian Killgore. The school district mandated vaccinations for all age eligible students on September 22, and three weeks later extended the requirement to teachers and anyone working on or visiting school campuses. Children aged 5-11 became eligible to receive the Pfizer covid vaccine on November 3, and the district’s vaccination policy immediately included them in the mandate. These students have until January 14 to provide proof of full vaccination (defined as two weeks after a second dose). The district will send families with students aged 5-11 directions for submitting proof of vaccination later this week.
